original_question: For n >= 2, describe the set of real numbers xi such that there are constants c_1(xi), c_2(xi) > 0 with uniform lower bounds for approximation by algebraic numbers of degree at most n, while infinitely many algebraic numbers of degree exactly n achieve the corresponding Dirichlet-type upper bound.
target_in_paper: Section 5.1, Question 5.2 (Bugeaud), the metric-problems question on real numbers badly approximable by algebraic numbers of bounded degree but still admitting infinitely many approximants at exponent n+1.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main ingredients of the target statement: an integer n >= 2, a set of real numbers xi, constants c_1(xi), c_2(xi) > 0 depending on xi, a uniform lower bound for approximation by algebraic numbers of bounded degree, and the existence of infinitely many algebraic approximants satisfying a matching upper bound at the same exponent scale.
missing_details: The paper does not ask for a broad description of the whole set; it defines a specific set A_n and asks whether A_n strictly contains the set of algebraic numbers of degree n+1.
The upper-bound approximants in the paper have degree <= n, not degree exactly n.
Both inequalities must be written explicitly with exponent n+1: |xi - alpha| >= c_2(xi) H(alpha)^(-(n+1)) and |xi - alpha| <= c_1(xi) H(alpha)^(-(n+1)).
H(alpha) must be defined: if f in Z[X] is the minimal polynomial of alpha, then H(alpha) = H(f) = max{|a_0|, ..., |a_d|}, the usual height.
Degree means algebraic degree over Q, i.e. [Q(alpha):Q].
The lower bound is quantified over all algebraic numbers alpha of degree <= n, whereas the upper bound is required for infinitely many such alpha.
The ambient set is a set of real xi, but the paper states the approximation inequalities for algebraic numbers alpha without explicitly restricting alpha to be real.

The paper's question is framed as a bounded-degree analogue of bad approximation by rationals inside Section 5.1 on metric problems, with the exponent n+1 aligned with the Wirsing-Schmidt scale discussed earlier in Section 4.2.
refined_question: For an integer n >= 2, let A_n be the set of real numbers xi such that there exist constants c_1(xi), c_2(xi) > 0 with the following properties: for every algebraic number alpha with [Q(alpha):Q] <= n, one has |xi - alpha| >= c_2(xi) H(alpha)^(-(n+1)); and there exist infinitely many algebraic numbers alpha with [Q(alpha):Q] <= n such that |xi - alpha| <= c_1(xi) H(alpha)^(-(n+1)), where H(alpha) denotes the usual height of the minimal polynomial of alpha over Z. Does A_n strictly contain the set of real algebraic numbers of degree n+1?
justification: The draft is aiming at the narrow metric question officially stated as Question 5.2, not at the broader metrical sets F_kappa and F'_kappa and not merely at the upper-bound statement of the Wirsing-Schmidt conjecture. Question 5.2 is the only place in the paper where the two-sided condition with constants c_1(xi), c_2(xi) is packaged into a set of real numbers and then compared with algebraic numbers of degree n+1. To make the question stand alone, one must import the definition of H(alpha) from Section 4 and spell out that the exponent is exactly n+1, matching the approximation scale highlighted in Section 4.2.
